title: How the Nature Index Tables Are Made
title_zh: 自然指数榜单是怎么做出来的
lead: Nature Index makes tables about science research. This guide explains how they made the 2026 tables about infectious diseases.
lead_zh: 自然指数会制作科研榜单。这份指南解释了2026年传染病榜单是怎么做出来的。

To find the articles, the team searched titles and abstracts. They used the Dimensions database. The search covered 83 infectious diseases. It also included 5 smaller groups for serious coronaviruses and flu types. The search words were the same as in 2021.

body:
The 2026 Nature Spotlight looks at infectious diseases. Its tables come from the Nature Index database. They cover articles about infectious diseases. These articles appeared in science and health journals from 2021 to 2025.

To find the articles, the team searched titles and abstracts. They used the Dimensions database. The search covered 83 infectious diseases. It also included 5 smaller groups for serious coronaviruses and flu types. The search words were the same as in 2021.

The team then kept only the articles that were also in the Nature Index database. These articles formed the final data set. The tables in this Spotlight are based on that data set.

The Spotlight is editorially independent. Advertisers have no influence over its content. You can read it in Nature Spotlight: Infectious diseases.

A guide to Nature Index tables
Information on the methodology used in the ranking for the 2026 Nature Spotlight: Infectious diseases.

The tables for the 2026
Nature Spotlight: Infectious diseases
are based on the
Nature Index database
and cover infectious-disease articles published in natural-science and health-science journals between 2021 and 2025.
Nature Spotlight: Infectious diseases
A keyword search on abstracts and titles was conducted to extract infectious-disease articles in Digital Science’s Dimensions database (Digital Science is part of Holtzbrinck, the majority shareholder of
Nature
’s publisher, Springer Nature). The search covered 83 infectious diseases and included 5 subcategories to cover severe coronaviruses and influenza subtypes. The
diseases and their Dimensions search strings
were the same as those for
Nature Index 2021 Infectious disease
. The Dimensions articles identified that were also in the Nature Index database formed the data set for the tables in this Spotlight.
